text: AI agents are starting to earn real money. But every one of them answers to a single owner. Koperasi changes that: an AI agent owned by a co-op of its members, where every rule lives on NEAR.

This is the live page. There is no server behind it: your browser reads the contract and the co-op's Sputnik DAO straight from NEAR testnet. The first panel answers one question. Who controls this agent? The members do, one vote each.

Don't trust us. Your browser checks. The by-laws the agent runs match the hash the members voted. The contract has no full-access key, not even the builder's, so its code changes only by a vote. And you can verify the model's Intel TDX and NVIDIA attestation yourself, against a nonce your own browser just made.
Every change the contract makes is a standard NEAR event, and this feed lists them as members act.

Members join through the DAO. Savings are NEAR staked in a pool the members chose, and contribution points reward the work they put in. The agent's prompt, model, prices and spending caps are its by-laws. A new version needs a vote, and the contract refuses any receipt made under other by-laws.

The agent sells work on NEAR AI Agent Market, runs its inference privately on NEAR AI Cloud, and leaves one receipt per job on chain. The market pays one human, the steward. So the steward posts a bond and serves a ninety-day term, and the audit compares every paid job with what reached the treasury. If earnings are seven days late, anyone can slash the bond.
Profit is shared by rule. The members vote each share, the contract splits it by savings and by contribution, and every member claims their own.

Small tasks are paid on trust that is earned on chain. A trusted contributor is paid with no vote, one member approves mid-sized work, and large tasks go to the whole DAO. Each payout is a DAO transfer the contract files itself, and every point on a record names where it came from.

Members also owe each other work, not only money. A member pledges a service, and whoever calls it in confirms it was kept. When a buyer disputes a job, three members in good standing are drawn at random as a jury. Here two of them upheld the case, and the contract refunded the buyer from the treasury, through DAO proposal sixty. The co-op even holds an Ethereum address with no private key anywhere. NEAR Chain Signatures sign for it only after a members' vote.
Every member gets a work record, read live from the chain: kept pledges, jury duty, paid tasks. Proof of work that nobody can type in.

This is what a member sees. Open proposals to vote on, the profit share they can claim, tasks to take, pledges to call in, and court cases to rule on. Invite links can carry a signed vouch, checked against the inviter's own key. And calls without a deposit go through the co-op's relayer, so members pay no gas.
Now a real transaction. Bob calls in the second unit of Alice's pledge, then confirms it was kept. Reload the page, and the chain already shows it: two of two called in, and Alice's standing went up.
You never have to take our word for any of it. npm run verify reads every claim in the README from the chain, with no keys and no transactions, and ends with: every claim checks out.

Koperasi is built on NEAR end to end. Sputnik DAO, Trezu templates, global contracts, signed vouches, gasless meta-transactions, Chain Signatures, NEAR AI Cloud and the Agent Market. The members own the agent. The chain keeps the receipts.
